title: Postprandial triglyceride response in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome: relationship with waist-to-hip ratio and insulin.
text_summary: 目的：与匹配的对照组相比，检查患有多囊卵巢综合征（PCOS）的女性餐后甘油三酯对高脂肪膳食的反应。设计：对照临床研究。结果：肥胖和非肥胖 PCOS 女性的腰臀比均高于对照组。结论：无论是否肥胖，PCOS 女性餐后高甘油三酯血症的扩大与较高的腰臀比和胰岛素抵抗有关，并有助于增加冠状动脉疾病的风险。

                   and Luisa Sa´nchez, M.D.b

                              Hospital Universitario de Los Andes and Universidad de Los Andes, Me´ rida, Venezuela

                           Objective: To examine the postprandial triglyceride response to a high-fat meal in women with polycystic
                          ovary syndrome (PCOS) compared with a matched control group.
                          Design: Controlled clinical study.
                             Setting: Department of Endocrinology and Pathophysiology, School of Medicine, Universidad de Los Andes.
                              Patient(s): 18 Hispanic women with PCOS (nine overweight and nine nonobese) and 9 healthy control women.
                             Intervention(s): Biometric measures and blood sample collection.
                     Main Outcome Measure(s): Insulin and glucose levels during a standard oral glucose tolerance test. Plasma
                                triglyceride, cholesterol, and high-density lipoprotein cholesterol levels were measured at baseline and at 4,
                                5, and 6 h after a high-fat meal.
                             Result(s): Both obese and nonobese PCOS women had higher waist-to-hip ratios than controls. PCOS
                    women had higher levels of fasting and postglucose insulin and fasting triglyceride and postprandial
                               triglyceride response and had lower levels of postprandial high-density lipoprotein cholesterol response, but
                        no signiﬁcant differences within PCOS groups were observed.
                           Conclusion(s): An expanded postprandial hypertriglyceridemia in PCOS women  is related to a higher
                              waist-to-hip ratio and insulin resistance, regardless of obesity, and contributes to increase the risk for coronary
                               artery disease. (Fertil Sterilt 2000;74:1159–63. ©2000 by American Society for Reproductive Medicine.)
                     Key Words: Polycystic ovary syndrome, Postprandial triglyceride, Insulin

                                                                 subjects with android body fat distribution, suggesting that
                                                          overweight per se was not the only determinant of the lipid
                                                              abnormalities in our PCOS women. This fact is particularly
                                                            important because the central distribution of body fat seems
                                                                   to be a better predictor of lipid abnormalities than is obesity
                                                                   in PCOS women.
                                                          Extended postprandial lipemia may increase the uptake of
                                                                    triglyceride-rich remnants by arterial cells (22) and thus
                                                                increase the atherogenic intracellular accumulation of cho-
                                                                       lesterol esters (23, 24). Our demonstration of an ampliﬁed
                                                               postprandial lipidemic response in overweight and nonobese
                                            women with PCOS completes the  list of metabolic and
                                                               vascular abnormalities associated with insulin resistance in
                                                                        this condition, contributing to increase the risk for coronary
                                                                   artery disease.
                                                                  In this study, we also conﬁrmed previous ﬁndings that
                                                               postprandial increase in triglyceride is directly related to its
                                                                   fasting plasma concentration (25) and plasma insulin levels
                                                                    (26). It is well established that both fasting (25, 26) and
                                                               postprandial (27, 28) plasma triglyceride concentration are
                                                                 correlated with plasma insulin concentration and insulin
                                                                    resistance. Consistent with previous observations (29, 30),
                                                                the PCOS patients had hyperinsulinism, which was indepen-
                                                             dent of the effect of obesity. Insulin resistance associated
                                                           with fasting dyslipidemia has been previously reported in
                                          PCOS patients (13). However, whether insulin directly mod-
                                                                   ulates the synthesis and secretion of intestinal lipoproteins or
                                                              plays a role in the regulation of the catabolism of triglycer-
                                                                   ide-rich lipoproteins is uncertain.
